title: Concurrency and parallelism: where the patterns break down

videos.script: Every pattern so far rested on something nobody said out loud. Between two lines of your code, nothing else runs. {{assumption}} This lesson takes that away. First, two words that people use as one. Concurrency is how a program is arranged. Parallelism is how it runs, on several cores at once. {{words}} You will time two kinds of slow work, waiting and computing, and see why Python threads help with one and not the other. {{timing}} Then four desks record four thousand loans, and the counter says about a thousand. No error, no warning. {{race}} A lock fixes it. Two locks taken in opposite orders freeze two desks, each waiting for the other. {{deadlock}} Then two patterns you already know, under threads. A singleton that builds four catalogues. An observer whose listener misses an event without a sound. {{patterns}} And a fix that needs no lock at all: values that cannot change. {{frozen}} Every program here runs on a real laptop, and some of its numbers move from run to run. That is part of the lesson. It ends with a way to choose a model of concurrency before you ever need a lock. {{choose}}
